templates.name: Personalized Cold Outreach
templates.description: Enrich a lead list, write a personalized first line for each prospect, verify deliverability, then drip follow-ups that stop the moment someone replies.

steps.name: enrich
steps.description: Resolve a real contact for each lead with Hunter — look up the named person, or surface a decision-maker when you only have the company.

steps.name: scrape
steps.description: Read each company's website for a few lines of context to personalize with.

steps.name: personalize
steps.description: Ask the live model to write one specific opener per prospect, falling back to a safe generic line when it returns nothing usable.

steps.name: verify
steps.description: Check each address for deliverability and drop the ones that would bounce before anything sends.

steps.name: launch
steps.description: Persist the campaign roster to a Postgres store the engine owns, then start the drip. A dry run stops here and returns the full plan without sending or persisting.

steps.name: send
steps.description: Deliver the current touch to everyone still active and log it, then pause at $0 until the drip interval elapses or a prospect replies.

steps.name: advance
steps.description: Wake on the reply-or-timeout, mark anyone who replied as done, then loop back for the next touch or end the run.

steps.name: done
steps.description: Return the campaign summary — who was enriched, how many were deliverable, what was sent, and who replied.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Works 3 built-in demo leads end to end: enrichment and verification are simulated for these fabricated companies, but the opener comes from a real model call and the first touch is a real, inspectable send to this agent's own Sapiom-hosted demo inbox. Pass your own `leads` to run a real campaign, including the multi-touch drip and reply-to-stop.

templates.name: Content Repurposing
templates.description: Turn one blog post or transcript into a tweet thread, LinkedIn post, newsletter, quote graphics, and a short clip — then email the whole pack.

steps.name: repurpose
steps.description: An LLM rewrites your source into every channel at once: the tweet thread, LinkedIn post, newsletter, pull-quotes, and a video script. If you set dryRun, it stops here and returns the copy.

steps.name: graphics
steps.description: Make one quote graphic per pull-quote, all at once, and save each one.

steps.name: clip
steps.description: Launch a video job that animates the first quote graphic into a short teaser clip, then pause until it finishes.

steps.name: collectClip
steps.description: Save the finished teaser clip.

steps.name: package
steps.description: Assemble the whole pack as one markdown document and upload it to file storage for a durable download link.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Email the pack to your recipient, or return it when no recipient is set. Ends the run with a summary of everything produced.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Repurposes the built-in sample post into copy plus real rendered quote graphics; skips the pricey teaser clip and emails nothing because no recipient is set.

templates.name: Dependency Upgrade
templates.description: On a schedule, a coding agent bumps a repo's dependencies in a sandbox, runs the tests, and pushes only when the build is green.

steps.name: plan
steps.description: Resolves the repo and the install and test commands and checks the input; with no repo it stops right away.

steps.name: bump
steps.description: Launches a coding agent to bump the repo's dependencies in a sandbox, then pauses until the run finishes.

steps.name: verify
steps.description: Re-attaches that sandbox and runs the install and test suite there; a failed run or a red build is rejected.

steps.name: assess
steps.description: Asks a model to rate the upgrade's risk from the dependency diff, holding anything above your bar.

steps.name: publish
steps.description: Pushes the bumped branch from the sandbox and archives the triage report.

steps.name: held
steps.description: The build was green but the risk was too high, so it archives the report and waits for a human.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: The coding run failed or the tests were red, so it archives the report and pushes nothing.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Runs a coding agent to triage upgrades and writes a report; pushes nothing (no repo).

templates.name: Self-Editing Writer
templates.description: Draft a piece against your brief, grade it against your own rubric with an LLM judge, and revise in a bounded loop until it clears the bar.

steps.name: parse
steps.description: Validate the brief and rubric, defaulting to a built-in sample, and seed the attempt counter.

steps.name: draft
steps.description: Write the piece from the brief — on a revision, address the rejected draft and the judge's critique too.

steps.name: judge
steps.description: Score the draft against your rubric with a second model call and parse a 0-to-1 score plus a critique.

steps.name: decide
steps.description: Compare the score to your threshold and the attempt count to the cap: below both, loop back to draft; otherwise publish. No model call here.

steps.name: publish
steps.description: The one terminal — return the final draft, whether it passed, the score, and how many attempts it took.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Drafts and grades the built-in sample brief against a rubric, revising once if needed, and publishes the final draft with its score.

templates.name: Website QA Crawler
templates.description: Crawl a site's pages, screenshot each one, audit content with a model, and check that Terms and Privacy links resolve.

steps.name: crawl
steps.description: Read the homepage's markdown and links, then crawl a bounded set of internal pages — prioritizing anything that looks like a Terms or Privacy link.

steps.name: render
steps.description: Open one browser session and screenshot every crawled page in it; a page that fails to render becomes a row, the rest are still captured.

steps.name: audit
steps.description: Ask a model to read every crawled page's content in one call and flag concrete content and structure issues.

steps.name: linkCheck
steps.description: Turn the crawl and render results into a link-integrity verdict: which pages didn't resolve, and whether Terms and Privacy are present and resolve.

steps.name: report
steps.description: Compile the screenshots, content findings, and link integrity into one QA report.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: Terminal off-ramp when siteUrl isn't a usable URL or the site can't be reached at all.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Crawls a bounded set of sapiom.ai pages, screenshots each one, audits the content with a model, and checks link integrity — reporting whatever it finds broken, including whether Terms and Privacy links resolve.

templates.name: Company News Roundup
templates.description: Search the web for a company's recent news, then publish a dated, illustrated roundup page to a small website for that company.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Search the web for the company's news from the last week. If nothing comes back, stop early and report no news instead of publishing.

steps.name: select
steps.description: Ask an LLM to pick the three-to-five most relevant articles and write a plain-language summary and an image prompt for each.

steps.name: illustrate
steps.description: Generate one image per selected article and save each to storage; an article whose image fails degrades to a text-only card.

steps.name: publish
steps.description: Save the dated page, rebuild the company's site from storage in a sandbox, and deploy it — returning the live site and page URLs.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Searches the web for a well-covered default company and publishes a dated, illustrated roundup page at a live sandbox URL; a company with no recent coverage ends in a distinct no-news terminal instead.

templates.name: Newsletter Autopilot
templates.description: On a weekly schedule, it researches a niche, writes and illustrates the issue, and emails it to your subscriber list.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Search the web for the niche and collect candidate sources.

steps.name: scrape
steps.description: Read the top candidates for their full article text, keeping just the snippet when a page won't load.

steps.name: write
steps.description: Hand the sources to an LLM to curate them and write this week's issue: a subject, a body that cites each source, and a header-image prompt.

steps.name: header
steps.description: Generate a header image for the issue; if none comes back, the issue still goes out without it.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Email each subscriber their own copy; a dry run, or a run with no subscribers set, returns the issue without sending.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Writes a newsletter from researched sources; sends to nobody (empty subscriber list).

templates.name: Ask Your Database
templates.description: Deploy a live endpoint that turns a plain-English question into a read-only SQL query and returns the answer.

steps.name: validate
steps.description: Checks the input (a database handle or connection string) and resolves config.

steps.name: resolve
steps.description: Reads the target Postgres connection string from a Sapiom database handle; on the built-in demo database it also seeds the sample schema so the query returns real rows.

steps.name: plan
steps.description: Translates the sample question into SQL with an LLM — or, for the built-in demo question, uses a fixed known-safe SELECT so the zero-setup path needs no model.

steps.name: guard
steps.description: Applies the read-only guardrail to the SQL; anything that isn’t a single read-only statement is rejected.

steps.name: execute
steps.description: Runs the guarded SELECT for real inside a READ ONLY transaction — statement-timeout-bounded and row-capped — and returns the actual rows.

steps.name: deploy
steps.description: Write the endpoint server into a sandbox and expose it at a stable URL, injecting DATABASE_URL and the endpoint’s own minted API key. With no key, nothing is deployed.

steps.name: deployed
steps.description: The endpoint is live — returns its URL plus the real rows from the sample query.

steps.name: deploy_failed
steps.description: The deploy failed — surfaces the deployPreview logs alongside the real sample rows already fetched.

steps.name: endpoint_skipped
steps.description: Without an API key of its own the endpoint is not deployed; the run still returns the real rows from the guarded sample query.

steps.name: query_failed
steps.description: The guarded query could not run against the database; nothing was deployed and the failing SQL is surfaced.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: Input or the sample SQL failed the guardrail; nothing was deployed.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Runs the built-in sample question against the seeded demo database for real rows, mints the endpoint its own scoped key, and deploys a working /query endpoint.

templates.name: Personalized Media Per Lead
templates.description: Read a table of leads and, per row, generate a personalized image or short clip, store it, and email each person a link — on a schedule.

steps.name: fetch
steps.description: Read up to `limit` recipient rows from a database table, seeding a demo table on the first run. If you set dryRun, it stops here and returns the rows and their prompts.

steps.name: renderImages
steps.description: For the image medium: make one personalized image per row, all at once, and save each.

steps.name: renderClip
steps.description: For the video medium: launch a short clip for one row, then pause until it finishes.

steps.name: collectClip
steps.description: Save the finished clip, then loop back for the next row, or move on once every row is done.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Email each recipient a link to their own asset; a dry run generates and sends nothing.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Renders personalized images; delivers nothing because no recipients are set.

templates.name: PR Review Bot
templates.description: When a pull request opens, a coding agent reviews the code and flags missing tests, then posts the review to your email or Slack.

steps.name: watch
steps.description: Register with the webhook source and pause until a PR opens — costing nothing while idle. With no source configured, review the built-in sample PR instead of waiting forever.

steps.name: review
steps.description: Wakes when a PR opens; its input is the PR payload. A coding agent checks the code out and analyzes the diff, flagging changes that lack tests.

steps.name: assess
steps.description: A model turns the coding agent's raw findings into a structured review — a verdict, a summary, and the list of missing tests.

steps.name: reportEmail
steps.description: Emails the review to the configured recipient.

steps.name: reportSlack
steps.description: Post the review to the configured channel with your Slack bot token. Without one, the review is returned in the run's output and nothing is posted.

steps.name: posted
steps.description: Return the result — the channel used and the verdict.

steps.name: failed
steps.description: The send errored; return the error.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Runs a coding agent to review the sample PR and returns a verdict; posts nothing (no webhook).

templates.name: Client Proposal Generator
templates.description: Draft a client proposal from a request, render it to a PDF, then wait for a person to approve it before it emails the client.

steps.name: draft
steps.description: An LLM turns the request into a structured proposal — title, summary, scope, and priced line items — then the totals are computed in code, not trusted from the model.

steps.name: render
steps.description: Spin up a sandbox, lay the proposal out as a PDF with a small Node script, save the file to storage, then tear the sandbox down.

steps.name: review
steps.description: Email the approver a summary and the PDF link, then pause and wait for their decision — costing nothing while idle. With no approver set, stop at the gate with the drafted proposal instead of waiting forever.

steps.name: onDecision
steps.description: Read the approval reply: approve emails the client, anything else stops safely with nothing sent.

steps.name: send
steps.description: The one outward step — email the approved proposal to the client. A dry run skips the send.

steps.name: pending
steps.description: No approver was set, so the run stops holding the drafted proposal and the signal that continues it. Nothing was sent, and nothing was approved.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: Rejected at review — nothing goes to the client, and the draft PDF stays on file.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Drafts the built-in sample brief into a priced proposal and renders it to a real PDF, then stops at the sign-off gate — no approver is configured, so nothing is emailed yet.

templates.name: Research Micro-Site
templates.description: Research a topic across the web, then build and deploy a shareable live report site — not just a document.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Take the topic and run one web search for candidate sources.

steps.name: scrape
steps.description: Read the top candidates for their full article text, keeping just the snippet when a page won't load.

steps.name: synthesize
steps.description: Hand the sources to an LLM to write a structured, cited report. A dry run — or a report too empty to build a site from — stops here and returns the report.

steps.name: build
steps.description: Launch a coding agent to build a self-contained static site from the report, then pause until it finishes — costing nothing while it works.

steps.name: publish
steps.description: Re-attach the coding agent's sandbox and deploy the site to a stable public URL.

steps.name: mapDomain
steps.description: If a domain you own is configured, point a subdomain at the live site with a free CNAME; otherwise this is skipped.

steps.name: live
steps.description: Return the live URL, the custom URL when one was mapped, the report title, and the sources.

steps.name: failed
steps.description: The build or the deploy failed; return the stage and the logs.

steps.name: drafted
steps.description: The dry-run off-ramp: the report was computed but nothing was built or deployed.

templates.name: Scene to Video
templates.description: Turn one scene description into a short, multi-shot video with a consistent style.

steps.name: decompose
steps.description: An LLM turns your scene into a style guide and an ordered shot list. A zero-setup run plans a single shot; pass dryRun to stop here and return just the plan.

steps.name: keyframe
steps.description: Launch an image job for one shot’s keyframe, then pause until it finishes.

steps.name: collectKeyframe
steps.description: Save the finished keyframe, then loop back for the next shot’s frame, or move on once every keyframe is in.

steps.name: animate
steps.description: Launch a video job that animates one keyframe into a clip, then pause until it finishes.

steps.name: collect
steps.description: Save the finished clip, then loop back for the next shot, or move on once every clip is in.

steps.name: stitch
steps.description: Join every clip with the synchronous merge endpoint; a single clip skips the merge, and a bounded polling fallback covers a provider that unexpectedly queues it.

steps.name: finalize
steps.description: Return the stitched video’s file id and download link.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Shoots the built-in sample scene as a single real keyframe and clip, and returns the finished video's download link.

templates.name: Scheduled Metrics Report
templates.description: On a schedule, query a database, write the narrative and render charts, then email the insight report.

steps.name: snapshot
steps.description: Resolve the target database (self-provisioning and seeding the demo DB if needed) and snapshot its current catalog metrics.

steps.name: detectAnomalies
steps.description: A model flags the one table most worth attention, trusting only labels the snapshot actually returned.

steps.name: narrate
steps.description: A model writes the narrative around the movement, leading with the flagged anomaly.

steps.name: followUp
steps.description: Run a parameterized read into the flagged table's recent write activity for a second, data-driven angle.

steps.name: chart
steps.description: Render the metrics and the follow-up read into a chart image in a sandbox and upload it.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Compile the report with the chart inline and email it to the configured recipient; with none set, return it in the run.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Snapshots the seeded demo database's own catalog, has a model flag the one table most worth attention, runs a second query into that table's write activity, writes a real narrative around both, and returns the full report with a rendered chart inline — nothing is emailed, because no `deliverTo` recipient is set.

templates.name: Scheduled Research Brief
templates.description: On a schedule, it researches a topic and emails you a short, sourced brief.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Search the web for the topic and collect candidate sources.

steps.name: scrape
steps.description: Read the top candidates for their full article text, keeping just the snippet when a page won't load.

steps.name: curate
steps.description: Hand the sources to an LLM to rank them, drop the weak ones, and write a short brief that cites each one.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Email the brief to your recipient; a dry run, or a run with no recipient set, returns it without sending.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Researches the topic, writes a sourced brief, and emails it to the agent's own Sapiom-hosted demo inbox; set deliverTo to send it to your address.

templates.name: Web Research Digest
templates.description: Search the web for a topic and get back a short, sourced digest.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Take the topic and run one web search, returning a synthesized answer and ranked results.

steps.name: summarize
steps.description: Format that answer and its source links into a markdown digest, in the run and with no model call.

setup.degradedWithoutSetup: Researches a default topic and returns a digest with cited sources.
